title: Grateful Dead Live at Milwaukee Auditorium on 1978-02-04
source: Set 2 Only; 7 Inch Half Track Nagra Reel Master @ 7.5 IPS; Recorded By Betty; Analog to Digital:By Dick Latvala(Technics 1506 Reel 2 Reel-Sony PCM R-500 DAT @ 44.1KHZ; DAT Zero-DAT#1 (Rob Bertrando); 100% flat transfer-DAT#2(JW) play back on Sony PCM R-500-Digital Audio Labs Carddeluxe-WAV @ 16bit 44.1 KHz; Editing(Adobe Audition CC)-FLAC Encoding(dBpoweramp)-Tagging(Tag & Re-name) by Jim Wise

ai_review.summary: Betty Cantor‑Jackson’s soundboard capture delivers crystal‑clear audio of a superb second set, highlighted by a haunting Black Peter and Donna’s soaring Dupree's Diamond Blues.
ai_review.review: The recording is universally praised for its unsurpassed, crisp sound quality – a true testament to Betty Cantor‑Jackson’s engineering.  The performance, though only the second set, is described as tight, energetic and featuring standout moments such as Black Peter and a memorable Donna‑Jean vocal on Dupree's Diamond Blues, making this a must‑hear for collectors.

ai_rating.rationale: All nine reviews are 4–5 stars with consistent praise for both the audio fidelity and musical performance, yielding a high combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear, crisp mix with no noticeable flaws; reviewers repeatedly call it “unsurpassed,” “awesome,” and “sweet sweet sound.”

show_quality.setlist_flow: Only the second set is present, but it flows tightly with an amped‑up feel, a unique NFA jam in the middle and a seamless transition into Donna’s vocal highlight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Several reviewers note Jerry’s storytelling (“good to hear JERRY tell that story again”) and his guitar tone as perfect.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum break is mentioned ("before the band breaks for Drumz") and the NFA jam follows it.
